Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the file. We saw the same spike on our side; it looks like a client-side retry loop that was introduced in a staging rollout on Sept 13 and then accidentally promoted. That caused a lot of duplicated token calls into the LLM for a subset of endpoints (mainly the summarization pipeline).

Two clarifying questions before the call:
- Can you show latency/SLO impact (p50/p95) during the spike window and whether any throttling/burst behavior from Redwood shifted performance?
- If we accept a short-term commit/bridge, can you outline what controls we get for burst credits and model fallback to reduce unit cost?

Procurement is cc'd; they want a simple bridge proposal and the redlines we anticipate. We're open to a 3–6 month bridge if it includes burst credits and an operational playbook so the next rollout doesn't repeat this.

Best,
Elena
Head of Platform
NovaForge

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Petrova <elena@novaforge.ai>, procurement@novaforge.ai
Date: 2026-10-16T07:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Q3 usage review + renewal options — analysis + proposal

Sooj — attaching the analysis and two quick artifacts: prefix-cache-report.pdf and a draft SLA amendment (SLA-amendment-draft.docx). Summary below for the external call:

- Root cause: client retry loop affecting summarization pipeline; duplicate requests increased token count by ~3.8x for affected flows between Sept 14–18.
- Latency/SLO: p50 increased from 85ms to 120ms during the peak; p95 moved from 320ms to 410ms. No cluster-wide throttling observed — traffic was within capacity but burst profile changed tail latency.
- Cache effectiveness: overall prefix/KV cache hit ~62% for summarization. Disabling cache during retries would have made the spike ~5–6x worse; caching saved ~28% of potential tokens. See attached PDF for endpoint breakdown.
- Proposed commercial path (sketch):
  * Option A (3-month bridge): 25% discounted committed volume (applied retro to spike window), 20% burst credits for anomalous days, standard SLA.
  * Option B (6-month bridge): 15% discounted committed volume, 40% burst credits, model-fallback allowance (auto-fallback to quantized variant for non-critical endpoints), and a 48-hour operational response SLA.

ROI recap (6-month example): with the model-mix adjustment and burst credits, projected 6-month token spend is ~12% lower vs unmanaged regeneration and we estimate a NPV-positive offset for NovaForge's feature roadmap when factoring reduced overage risk.

Next steps for Wed call: I'll present the analysis and recommended Option B as the preferred path given the customer desire for operational controls. Monica — please have the playbook ready to share as a Google Doc link. Ben — if we land on Option B, can you draft the DocuSign template and proposed redlines for procurement?

— Karthik
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: prefix-cache-report.pdf (PDF, 420 KB); SLA-amendment-draft.docx (DOCX, 36 KB)

Thanks — the analysis is helpful and addresses our immediate concerns. After internal review procurement is willing to proceed with Option B (6-month bridge) pending a final SLA amendment and DocuSign.

Two final asks before we sign:
1) Please include explicit language for burst credit redemption (how credits apply to overages) and an example invoice line item.
2) Add a short runbook appendix that lists the client-side fixes we expect NovaForge to implement and the verification steps Redwood will use to confirm the fixes.

If you can push the final SLA amendment + DocuSign link by EOD Friday we will route internally and aim to sign next week.

Elena
Head of Platform
NovaForge
